text:
Nick Suzuki's ironman streak ended in October when a hand injury cost him a couple of weeks, and Montreal's captain has looked like himself since returning on Nov. 5. He has 20 points in 17 games, 8 of them on the power play, and he's playing almost 21 minutes a night against the other team's best. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 99th percentile last season, the same season he won the Selke.

Some of this is inflated. Montreal has scored 5.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and he's shooting 19.6% against a league norm of 13.3%. His last ten (11 points against 11.4 expected) are right where they should be, though, which tells you the engine is fine and the on-ice bounces are the extra.

What to watch is the power play. Suzuki said "it's definitely not broken" before a loss to the Rangers, as Eric Engels of Sportsnet posted, and it went quiet that night. He's still the one setting it up: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 89th percentile for primary shot assists.
headline: The captain is back, and so is the machine
